summary: In Greek mythology, Maron (Maro) is the hero of sweet wine — priest of Apollo at Ismarus in Thrace, son of Euanthes (and in some notices grandson of Dionysus and Ariadne). Odysseus spares him when sacking the Ciconian city and receives from him the powerful unmixed wine later used against Polyphemus. Maroneia was named for him as founder and vine-warden.

sections.heading: Wine of Ismarus
paragraphs: In Odyssey 9 Odysseus carries a goatskin of dark sweet wine given by Maron son of Euanthes, priest of Apollo who watched over Ismarus. Odysseus' men had protected Maron, his wife, and child when they sacked the Ciconians; in return Maron gave gold, a silver mixing-bowl, and twelve jars of divine unmixed wine. That wine makes the Cyclops Polyphemus drunk.
Later authors expand him as companion or pupil of Dionysus/Silenus, expert in planting and pruning vines so that farmers see Maron handsome among the grapes at Ismaros.

sections.heading: Maroneia
paragraphs: The Thracian city Maroneia took its name from Maron as founder; Diodorus has Osiris/Dionysus leave the aged Maron there to tend the plants he introduced. Euripides' Cyclops also knows Maron in the wine tradition. Atlas id maron-thrace is this Ismaran priest-hero — not unrelated later namesakes.
